There are professionals who specialize in ceiling fans. Many models can be oiled while still attached to the ceiling. If you are simply unable to access the oil hole, then you will need to remove the fan from the ceiling, which is a bit more complicated! To attach the screws, you will turn them clockwise.[[Image:Oil a Ceiling Fan Step 18.jpg|center]]

Once reinstalled, test your fan on a slow setting to ensure it’s properly connected and balanced.<ref>[v161475_b01]. 15 July 2020.</ref> Turn on the power to the room by switching back the breaker so that you can test the fan. added: Ceiling fans can wear over time, requiring them to be taken down for routine maintenance. If your ceiling fans starts making a lot of noise, the oil reservoir may be too low for optimal operation. Check to ensure your fan requires oil and then drip oil into the bearings to oil it.
== Steps ==
=== Checking Oil Levels ===
#Check to see if your ceiling fan runs with an oiled motor. Some fans don’t use oil at all, so don’t assume that the fan must be oiled.<ref> http://ceilingfans.hansenwholesale.com/?cat=5</ref>
#Find the manual for your model. Read through the instructions about how to oil it. Look for instructions about checking oil levels.
#Make sure the power is turned off to your ceiling fan. Set up a stepladder so that you can check the oil while it is still installed in the ceiling.
#Insert a pipe cleaner into the oil level hole. Then, stick a pipe cleaner in the oil level hole to use as a dipstick.
#*If the pipe cleaner comes out with oil on it, then oiling the fan will not solve your problem.
#*If the pipe cleaner is inserted completely and it doesn’t touch oil in the reservoir, you should oil your fan.<ref> http://www.hunterfan.com/SupportDocuments/OwnersManuals/41121.pdf</ref>
#Purchase a small can of 3-in-1 oil or WD-40 spray.
=== Oiling Your Ceiling Fan ===
#Insert a Phillips head bit into your cordless screwdriver. Grab a stepladder to gain access to the fan.
#Disconnect the ceiling fan from the ceiling by unscrewing the fan blades, followed by the fan motor. You may need help from a friend to hold the fan blades as you take them down.
#Set the motor down on a table. Find the bearings at the top and the bottom of the motor.
#Turn the motor right side up. Drip three to four drops into the top bearing. Then, spin the motor around about 10 times so that the oil works into the bearings.
#*If you are using WD-40 use a short spray directly into the bearings, and then turn the motor to work it into the motor.

#Turn the motor up side down. Squeeze or spray three drops of oil into the bottom bearing, where the blades connect to the motor. Turn the bottom section of the motor 10 times to work the oil into the bearings.
#Reconnect your motor to the ceiling, starting with electrical wiring and finishing with the screws.
#Reconnect the fan blades one by one. Once reinstalled, test it on a slow setting to ensure it’s properly connected and balanced.
== Tips ==

*It is recommended that you check the oil reservoir and oil the fan each time you move the location of the fan. When the fans is tipped and moved, oil can easily leak out of the reservoir. Do it just before reinstallation.
== Things You'll Need ==
*Step ladder
*Pipe cleaner
*Owner’s manual
*WD-40 or multi-purpose oil
*Cordless drill
*Phillips head drill bit
